plan.trigger: More than one credible implementation path exists.
plan.artifact: Record chosen path, rejected alternatives, risks, and verification.

security.trigger: Identity, permissions, audit, settlement, sandboxing, secrets, CI, or release automation changed.
security.artifact: Independent security review notes before integration.

fan_out.trigger: Work spans more than three crates, apps, or service boundaries.
fan_out.artifact: Split scope or assign disjoint ownership.

test_expansion.trigger: New public behavior has only happy-path coverage.
test_expansion.artifact: Failure-mode tests or an explicit tracked gap.

docs.trigger: Public commands, types, protocols, setup, architecture, status, or claims changed.
docs.artifact: Docs update in the same change.

escalation.trigger: Credentials, destructive operations, production deploys, legal/governance/financial decisions, or contradictory human direction.
escalation.artifact: Human blocker record and an unblocked continuation path.

definitionOfDone: Behavior exists in code or the unsupported claim is removed.
Failure modes are tested or explicitly tracked.
A fresh human or agent can resume from tracked context.

afterSuccessfulPush: If it names an unblocked task, continue into that task immediately instead of ending with a status report.
If the named task is blocked by unrelated dirty files, record that blocker in the task and select the next unblocked task.
Stop only when every candidate is blocked, the user explicitly asks to pause, or an external turn boundary prevents further work.
